paper_metadata.title: Refinement of Microstructures and Improvement of Mechanical Properties in Intermetallic TiAl Alloys by Rheocasting

The molten charge was continuous- ly cooled under the condition of no heating of the isother- mal furnace to achieve the maximum cooling rate of the charge. Then, the stirrer began to rotate immediately after the insertion of it into the molten alloy, continued to rotate for the maximum period of 30 s, and was removed from the semi-solid alloy.

mechanisms.name: fragmentation of lamellar structure by mechanical stirring

evidence.quote: It was recognized that the drastic refinement of primary crystals is not owing to the difference in cool- ing rate occurred in the solidification processes with and without the stirrer inserted into the melt, but owing to the fragmentation of lamellar structure with rotational stirring.
It was considered that this large elongation is achieved by dynamic recrystallization during deformation of the tensile testing at 1273 K.

mechanisms.name: release of high strain energy by reheating

evidence.quote: Reheating in the high-frequency furnace released the high strain energy built up in the charge by the forced stirring, which, in turn, prevented the occurrence of cracks in the cooling process of the rheocast intermetallic TiAl alloy.

conflicts.description: Abstract states high-temperature tensile strength increases with increasing temperature (solidified without stirring), while Table 1 shows 320 MPa at 1073 K and 389 MPa at 1273 K; the text in Section III.4 also states strengths 'increased with increasing temperature' though this wording is inconsistent with the abstract statement on improvement over reference alloy.

evidence.quote: The tensile strengths at elevated temperature increased with increasing temperature from 1073 K to 1273 K in the Ti-44%Al alloy solidified without stirring, as shown in Table 1.
